mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen for three consecutive weeks (-24.3 to -17.7), indicating a steady return of commuting activity. This commuting recovery typically spills over into retail and recreation visits along commute routes, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES having risen in each of the last three weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 9.7 to 7.9 points over four weeks, a sign that people are spending less time at home out of caution. If RESIDENTIAL falls below 7.0 points, this signals a behavioral threshold where reduced home-dwelling converts directly into higher discretionary retail outings, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +7.0 points in a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise, or falls, in the two weeks following a weekly RESIDENTIAL reading below +7.0 points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both improved in the last two weeks (TRANSIT -25.4 to -23.6; WORKPLACES -19.4 to -17.7). When both commuting-linked series rise together, the joint recovery of mobility infrastructure and job-site attendance compounds to drive a stronger rebound in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose concurrently for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is highly volatile (-33.1, -22.1, -32.7, -32.0), consistent with transient cherry-blossom-season outdoor activity in mid-April Tokyo. As the seasonal flowering period ends, outdoor park visits should fall sharply, and that foot traffic will redirect toward retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops more than 10 points week-on-week after a seasonal peak
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the two weeks following a PARKS week-on-week decline exceeding 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has been flat at -23.1 for two consecutive weeks after an earlier improvement, suggesting behavioral fatigue or a plateau in discretionary outings. This stagnation pattern, absent new stimulus from commuting or transit series, implies RETAIL_REC will remain flat or drift lower over the next four weeks rather than continue rebounding.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change is within 1 point for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days rises meaningfully above the prior 28-day mean despite two weeks of near-zero week-on-week change.

mechanism_narrative: The steady narrowing of TRANSIT's deficit from -28.7 to -23.6 over four weeks is consistent with a policy-loosening regime (reduced travel advisories or capacity limits). Under such a regime, continued transit normalization mechanically enables greater retail and recreation access, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT continuing its four-week improving trend, indicating the regime assumption is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility reverses and falls by more than 5 points week-on-week after its recent recovery (-24.3 to -17.7), this would signal a renewed policy tightening (e.g., reinstated work-from-home guidance) that would suppress associated retail and recreation trips within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week of a WORKPLACES week-on-week drop exceeding 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has worsened slightly over the last two weeks (-11.6 to -14.4) while RETAIL_REC stayed flat, suggesting households are consolidating errands rather than expanding broader retail and recreation outings. When essential-trip mobility (GROCERY_PHARM) deteriorates alongside flat RETAIL_REC, combined caution signals suppress discretionary retail recovery over the next four weeks more than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM worsens for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC remains flat
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM worsening for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC being flat in the prior period.
